acceptanceCriteria: Route and Auth composition remains exactly owned by accepted ADR-0015/P17: an application installs zero or one credential resolver backed by an explicit Service; the resolver produces Principal only; Context Resolution produces application scope; Policy authorizes; Better Auth remains an ordinary reference integration and QUESTPIE gains no core Auth schema, migrations, server, session, client, or UI.

Action becomes the single public owner of one external or nondeterministic invocation. It owns exact input, inferred output with optional pin, declared errors, Policy, exposure, cancellation, and explicit ambiguity; its Context has immutable Execution facts, effect Services, and generated Query/Mutation callers but no data/transaction facade, raw database, durable controls, or System elevation. Effect Identity is invocation metadata: direct callers supply it, Reaction or Job derives it, step.action binds it from Job run plus ordered checkpoint name, the handler receives effect.id, and checkpoint authors cannot override it as domain input.

Ordinary Action invocation never retries automatically. Reaction or Job owns durable acceptance and stable Effect Identity; provider idempotency and receipt lookup remain explicit provider/application contracts, and an unknowable outcome remains ambiguous.

QUESTPIE exposes one versioned Job Resource over the accepted durable run/attempt/lease kernel and removes Workflow, defineWorkflow, a Workflow client, and any second workflow runtime from current and deferred public scope.

An ordinary Job and a checkpointed Job use the same Definition, handler, run, attempt, lease, worker, and event vocabulary. A Job that uses no checkpoint command creates no checkpoint history or second runtime protocol.

The closed Job checkpoint helper admits only named generated Mutation, named generated Action, durable sleep, and typed signal wait. It admits no arbitrary callback. Checkpoint name is a stable ordered identity distinct from the closed typed signal name.

Checkpoint history retains Job identity, required semantic version, executable digest, ordered checkpoint name, canonical command digest, stable Mutation Call Identity, and stable Action Effect Identity plus receipt or explicit ambiguity. Incompatible code refuses claim; latest-code replay is forbidden.

Cron is a compiler-owned schedule attached to Job over PostgreSQL durable state, not a second Resource or scheduler abstraction. Every scheduled instant has one stable tick identity; concurrent acceptance converges once; schedule removal stops future ticks and preserves already accepted runs.

The generated browser client may include network-exposed Actions but includes neither Routes nor a generic Job control plane. Applications expose selected Job request, status, cancel, and signal behavior through ordinary Policy-protected Operations.

A repository-aware broad Workflow/defineWorkflow scan classifies every current root authority, ADR, top-level v4 product document, public v4 guide, design-fiction source, permanent capability/proof map, and architecture visual. Every discovered path is either in the exact post-PASS projection or is a byte-falsifiable ordinary-process exemption containing no durable Workflow product marker.

The executable model demonstrates contract coherence only. PostgreSQL crash windows, ten-instance cron races, signals, cancellation, bounded history, direct/network parity, generated client boundaries, rolling compatibility, and declaration/load budgets remain explicit implementation acceptance gates and are not claimed as implemented by this proof.

This candidate changes only its decision, structured projection, three compile-only interface/type prototypes, executable model and browser, validator, negative controls, manifest, and preserved raw BLOCKED review. It does not project authority, edit an Accepted ADR, change public docs, or modify production source before a fresh stateless Opus-medium PASS.
